title: Normalized finite scalar coordinates on modules and strict towers
statement: Let $W$ be a scheme and work on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $a:R\to S$ be commutative ring sheaves, let $U$ be restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and choose $b:R^d\simeq U(S)$, $d\in\mathbf N$. Use the sheafified scalar tensor and its cochain-unit-normalized left derived functor [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] [def-pur-change-of-rings-complex], and finite powers of complexes [lem-pur-finite-power-complex]. Define the ordinary natural coordinate isomorphism $U(S\otimes_R M)\simeq M^d$ as the unique one whose $j$th coordinate on every local pure tensor $s\otimes x$ is $\lambda_j(s)x$, where $\lambda_j$ is the $j$th coordinate of $b^{-1}$. Finite freeness makes scalar extension exact. Define the derived coordinates by exact localization, normalized on every cochain scalar counit. Make the same constructions on whole strict $\mathbf N^{\mathrm{op}}$-diagrams and their ordinary derived categories [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations]: the ordinary formula is imposed at every diagram index, the exact localized scalar functor has its canonical whole-cochain factor, and the derived coordinates are uniquely fixed by that factor and by localization of the ordinary coordinates followed by the canonical finite-product comparison. All constructions include $d=0$.

proof.text: Generalize the private finite-basis helpers of FiniteFreeScalarExtension to separate object and morphism universes. Evaluate the specified basis isomorphism on each object of the site. The resulting linear equivalence S(V) ≃ R(V)^d induces S(V) ⊗ M(V) ≃ M(V)^d, with jth component λ_j(s)x on pure tensors. Pure-tensor induction proves compatibility with restriction maps and naturality in M. The tensor presheaf is thus a finite product of sheaves, so its sheafification unit is an isomorphism. Transport the coordinate isomorphism through this unit and through the prescribed ordinary extension object equalities. Pure-tensor induction after precomposition with the unit proves uniqueness. The argument uses only finite product projections, so it includes d=0.

Restriction of scalars reflects isomorphisms through the forgetful functor to abelian sheaves. It preserves finite limits and colimits. Since the restricted scalar extension is naturally finite power, an exact functor, reflection gives exactness of scalar extension.

An exact ordinary scalar extension inverts quasi-isomorphisms. The universal left-derived counit is therefore invertible; compose it with the quotient-to-derived comparison to identify the prescribed derived extension on cochains. Localize the ordinary natural coordinates, followed by the finite-power complex comparison and the product comparison for Q. Localization lifts this natural isomorphism uniquely; its component formula is exactly the required cochain-counit normalization.

Apply the ordinary coordinate isomorphism at each index of an entire strict diagram. The pointwise product comparison identifies this diagram with its categorical finite power; projection naturality proves compatibility with transition maps and pure-tensor extensionality gives uniqueness. Extension and restriction are exact pointwise. Apply the same localization construction to these entire diagram categories, using their canonical exact-localization factor. Localization uniqueness gives the required derived whole-diagram normalization before any evaluation.
